tips.comment: Gwennie May Jem has a 10 lbs penalty to contend with after landing back-to-back wins last time out. This runner has been in fine form and looks to have enough improvement to defy the penalty.

Prospect House won here after a short break in April but did not get on with the step up in trip to 2m4f when third last time out. I think the return here at 2m1f and just 3 lbs heavier than that last win could see him bounce back.
Second last time beaten favorite, going to suit, jockey claiming seven pounds. Excellent each way chance at 13/2. Will be there at the business end of the race, nap each way.

Was once with W. Mullins but got discarded when beaten into 2nd by a 40/1 shot when odds on. That form isn't that bad as the winner is now rated 108 in Ireland. Foreverwalking is rated 98 here in the UK, so should be winning 0-100 races like this. This stable likes a small gamble, and the horse has been punted on twice in its last three races. So look closely to the off to see if there's any money for it. I think there will be as he comes into this on top weight. Looks a decent e/w bet at 14s.
Has yet to win a chase, but it's hard not to be interested in him even at this short price after the way he won his latest race over the smaller obstacles at this course last month.

Very consistent and very rarely runs a bad race. Travels well and jumps for fun. Always in the mix at the business end. Was 2nd, beaten only half a length over CD last month, so should be in the mix again. The 11/1 looks a sound e/w bet here.

Zmiinyi has been placed in two chases and a point-to-point race from twelve starts. Fell in a chase over 2m at Warwick on his latest outing in April. He is wearing cheekpieces for the first time today. Upped in trip to 2m 5f should suit. Seems well treated and with a clear round could well be able to win this race.

The model I run suggests an upset can be caused by Higgs. This result has been predominantly driven by Higgs having a comparable RPR to the rest of the runners here, but an official ranking leaving him carrying significantly less weight than most of the other runners. The current odds-on market favorite carries almost 2 stone (!) more in weight around this 2m 5f trip. Higgs has shown some glimpses of getting over the line first with figures of 423-33, and maybe this could suit. The market favorite is trying fences again for the first time in nearly a year from hurdles. The model issued a 'very low' staking indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.
A Skelton runner, and they do well here at Market Rasen. Who won on debut and best form of these should be there or thereabouts.

The model I run suggests Celestron Star can win this one. Celestron Star comes here in good form, having come first when last running 23 days ago, and looks to add to that here. Luke Scott on board claims 5 lbs, which keeps Celestron Star competitive from a weights perspective in which a lot of claiming jockeys are running. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator, which translates to a 0.5pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

I'm taking a chance with this one, purely because of the yard's form. The mare may be able to improve on her run three weeks ago, which was itself an improvement on previous efforts. A wind operation and tongue tie seem to have helped her.

Im A Believer is a four-year-old taking on his elders in this bumper, and his five-pound weight-for-age allowance should be sufficient for him to get his first win, having finished 2nd at Plumpton in his only race so far.
This quite expensive gelding didn't show much on his debut, but now trying a tongue strap and with the yard in decent nick, a step up can be expected.

The model I run suggests Letterston Lady can win this one. All the runners line up here with an RPR that's only 3 points difference, but Letterston Lady looks to be well treated off this official ranking. Lines up here with a weight to carry that looks very manageable around this 2m 4f trip. Champion jockey Sean Bowen picks up the reins, and Letterston Lady is also a previous course winner and distance winner. Comes here in good form after a decent first 24 days ago. The model has issued a 'very low' stakes indicator largely as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation. This translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

Prince Imperial has been in fine form since September, winning 4 out of 6. Would have been 5 but was headed in the final strides. A 2lb rise should be manageable. Good chance to get back to winning ways.

This gelding appears to be improving, and with the yard hitting a bit of form, I'm expecting a good run. He's gone up 5 lb in the weights, but his attitude is something that not all horses display. He is determined, and that counts for more than a few pounds.
Bannister has winning form last year, including a course handicap here in September, and followed up with a second place. Shaped well on reappearance 17 days ago, so should be fit.

This is quite the price for a last-time-out winner. The nine-year-old got to the front too soon at Uttoxeter last month and I honestly think that race was as good as this one. The stable are flying and a 3lb rise in the ratings is workable. A cracking each-way price if you can get 3 places.

Market House has spent most of this year on the flat with three wins under his belt. His sole run hurdling was a decent third when finding 2m4f a bit too far. The drop to 2 miles today could bring more improvement.
Has made steady, if not spectacular, progress over the hurdles and now handicapping should be more competitive. The stable is in good form, so every chance today.

Gms Prince looks to have restored his confidence on the last two starts since falling heavily at the last here three starts ago when he could possibly have won. Back at the same mark today and likely to be asked for a full effort today, he has strong place claims at the very least.

The model I run suggests Square Du Roule can win this one. Square Du Roule lines up here with the highest RPR of the 8 runner field and has an official ranking that leaves him kindly treated in the weights, carrying over a stone less than the top weight. Placed well 19 days ago and can get over the line first here today. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

It must be very difficult for the layers to price up a horse coming back from a stint in point to points, but St Patrick's Bridge was once rated 112 two years ago before going pointing and is now down to a mark of 99, it's last two runs in ptps were a first, and then a 2nd to a multiple winner, so comes here in good form, and this is a weak 0-100 race and just sneaks in, also has a 2nd to his name at this course in his earlier days. I'm going for a straight win here at 4/1 because nothing should beat him with a clear round of jumping.

Tried to make all over 2 and a half miles at Wincanton under today's jockey when last seen in March 20235 but headed close to home and runner-up. Not seen since but brought a long way for this by Sue Gardner and could go one better on first run following recent wind surgery.

Matoury had its first run for over 400 days just over three weeks ago, and the 6-year-old looked in good shape (3rd to Iron Heart, who runs earlier today) and is sure to benefit from the outing. It has been 3rd at this track in 3 out of 4 runs and has no issues with the quicker ground. Maggs gets in the saddle and claims 5lb. He has an exceptional riding record at this course (6 wins and 4 seconds in 20 rides). The price offers good EW value.

Shantou Lucky last won in September off an 86 with Aaron in the saddle. Although a bit duff since, I think he could be back in the game today off an 85 after wind surgery with Aaron and his claim back on top. He might need another run yet, but still worth a chance today.

Lazzar looks ready to get off the mark after a couple of solid runs this spring. He was a close second at Kempton and then a good third at Windsor, both over six furlongs. Dropping back to five and a bit here might sharpen him up, and in a small field with no standout rivals, this looks like his best chance yet to get his head in front.

This gelding, who has raced twice, has taken a considerable step forward since his first outing. He came 2nd out of 10 in a novice race at Wolverhampton 14 days prior, with the expected progress, he stands a good chance of winning.

I had this race between this one and Blackbrook, with preference just for the former. The 4th over C&D last time out was when the jockey didn't do very much right, in truth, and he was still only beaten 3 lengths. That was a catalogue of errors from the jockey, and the switch to David Egan is a big positive for me. He also has some recent stats for this quirky course. The horse races off the same mark here and will surely be given a better ride, so he looks a good bet to me.

Blackbrook has been unplaced in four starts so far, but we might not have seen the best of this one just yet. The yard does well here with what they have, and there has been support for this one, so a big run is expected.
Good last time out and has ample stamina and speed over this distance. The trainer and jockey today are a positive and can get the best out of him in this field.
Trained locally and has seen money this evening. Down 4lb since last run and with 7 more for a very capable Jack Dace, then must have an each-way chance.

Small each-way tip for this horse, a slow start didn't help last time out, finished 4th of 5 over 1m2f at this course , better run the time before that so he might be worth one more chance in this very open looking race. Drop in trip here may be more suitable.

Twilight Guest finally got his head in front over this course and distance last week, winning with plenty in hand. He’s turned out quickly under a 5lb penalty, but that might not be enough to stop him if he’s in the same mood. With confidence high and conditions to suit, he’s got a strong chance of following up.

A course and distance winner, and has run his best races at Brighton, which is not the easiest course to run at. Steps back in distance here, and the handicap mark has been dropping after every run and drops below his last winning mark of 55.

Cryptos Dream returns to Brighton, a track where she’s previously notched two wins over this trip. Her recent efforts on the all-weather have been respectable, including a close third at Chelmsford and a fourth at Wolverhampton. Now back on turf and racing off a mark of 51, she’s below her last winning rating, which could make her competitive in this field.

Walk The Moon is possibly Tony Carroll's second string here but I'm not sure that he is. Has done a lot of his running on the all-weather but recent runs on the flat on fastish going have been encouraging. The fact that there's a slight drop in trip as well may also suit. Worth an each-way play

The 5yo is a previous 5.5f C/D winner. He was unlucky four weeks ago over the C/D after coming off a 6 month break, losing out in the last 25 yards but clear of the rest. He should be a big player now dropping into a low grade 0-50 rated classified stakes.

Apple’s Angel, a 3yo filly, gets a helpful weight allowance and showed promise when third just days ago. She’s lightly raced and open to improvement at this level. With a decent draw and a capable rider, she could go close if building on that last effort. Each-way value at 8/1 in a low-grade sprint where little stands out.

Wasn't quite at best form on her last run on Turf but she arrives for today's race is slightly better form than last time, capable of better. Current rating looks fair , horses from this trainer often run well at this course.
Local Bay was racing and winning off higher marks last season. He ran good races the last two times. He's due to strike anytime soon.
The drop back to the mile distance should see this fare a lot better after finding the 10 furlongs too stamina-sapping. The trainer does well here and I expect a better run this afternoon.

A nice run from the 5yo mare two weeks ago, a close 2nd of 10 and she easily had the measure of the rest. She was coming off a 5 month break and should be better for the run. This handicap is not as strong. She’s effectively 2lb better off now with a good claiming apprentice booked for the ride.

Kessaar Power ran into a winner the system threw up in Crowd Quake last time out and only found that one too good. Will take some beating here back in similar company and looks a likely winner again before too long.
Bear to Dream has some speed and likes Brighton. Not shown best yet and I think will show some application over this distance. Not outclassed in this field.

Letter Of The Law looks to have a few things going for him here, he loves the track, the trainer is in good form and he was a good 2nd at Chepstow lto, the 1st & 3rd from that race both won on next start so the form looks good. Front runners are generally favoured at this on this ground round here and he should be up there if not making it

Mudlahhim is a winner at this trip in the past and might be capable of running a big race in this company. The selection ran well over this trip at Wolverhampton last time and should transfer that to a turf surface here.

Blue Collar Lad has run a lot on the All Weather and over 7f with mixed success. But today, back on the turf, we will see a better effort. Both runs at Brighton, Blue Collar handled the track well and wasn't far off the win. So I expect similar today for at least a place.

Has disappointed last twice, but was in good form on 2 prior runs on Aw. However, is a C/D winner so just as able on turf, is not going to get many better opportunities than this classified apprentice stakes off current mark of 46, good apprentice up allowed 7lb and in hands of a very shrewd trainer, making current 20/1 very good Ew value in the race.
Blue Orbit, a 2-year-old bay colt, ran well on debut. It looks like the extra furlong here would be ideal. The trainers have had a few winners and places, so expect a big run.
With trainer and jockey in good form, worth a punt as this one makes its debut as a half-brother to several winners.

Race 2 at Windsor today is a Novices (Class 4) for 2-year-olds over 1,218m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 2yo gelding Bring It On from the Tom Dascombe yard. It will be ridden by Pierre-Louis Jamin. This son of Dandy Man had a decent debut, finishing 2nd over the 5 furlongs at Thirsk just over a month ago. He gave the impression that further would be needed, which is what he gets here. With the expected improvement, he should be a top challenger here.
Musical Soldier a 2 year old bay colt making his debut here for Ollie Sangster. The trainer seems to have a decent group,of 2 year olds this season. Might be worth an each way punt here.

Small each-way tip for this horse. Others have more experience so they have a slight advantage. Adalida makes her debut for a trainer who often does well with his newcomers and for now, this distance looks ideal for this horse. Top jockey is booked

Jettie’s Run returns to action at Windsor after signing off last season with a tidy win at Kempton. She beat a filly who’s since placed in Listed company, so that form stacks up nicely. She’s got a 7lb penalty to carry here, but with Ralph Beckett’s yard in good form and Rossa Ryan booked, she looks the one to beat. If she’s trained on, she could be a cut above this field.
Strong debut that hints at a lot to come. Balanced form and the Cox yard is going really well. Suited to the distance and going.

Improved on its debut run last time out when upped to the 6 furlongs. Another trainer that does well here, and once again, significant jockey booking suggests they fancy this one's chances this evening.

The Jonathan Portman-trained Newfangled has been running consistently well this year, winning twice from 5 runs. His figures read: 32131. This good form hasn't gone unnoticed by the handicapper, going up from his 3rd place off 64 in March 25 to 69, winning over C&D 9 days ago. I think he has another win in him in this grade off his current mark of 71. Winning jockey Rob Hornby, who knows him well, is in the saddle, and another big run is on the cards.

Savvy Exchange lines up at Windsor and could be primed for a better showing. He was well beaten at Chelmsford last time but that was his first run in five months, so he’s entitled to come on for it. His earlier form includes a narrow second at Redcar and a maiden win at Pontefract, suggesting he’s capable at this level. With Hollie Doyle booked and a decent draw in stall 2, he might outrun his odds.

Previous course and distance winner. 5th in the race last year. Is drawn well in stall 5. Good race to aim at from there. Top jockey on board in Jim Crowley, who has won on the horse before. Solid chance at Windsor.
Two good runs this season since joining yard over 10f shaping as though drop in trip might suit. Race could be run to suit and could take a step forward here in first time tongue strap.
Still low mileage on this one's clock and is unexposed for a 4-year-old. Having its first outing for this stable, and their runners here do well, so it could make the frame at decent-looking odds.

Racing Demon has found himself an excellent opportunity to bounce back here was last seen at Newbury 17 days ago where finishing 10th/13 however that was just his second start after a 160 day break and now arrives here in top fitness and ready to get competitive currently operating on a very dangerous mark of 63 E De Giles's inmate looks poised to strike here and worth noting he has now dropped 2lb below his last winning mark likely to be well positioned in this 7 horse field coming out of gate 1 here at Windsor raxing on ideal ground ideal ground conditions here Racing Demon can bounce back and is more than capable of taking a class 5 handicap of this nature jockey Luke Morris takes the ride and can give Racing Demon a promising ride here at Windsor must enter calculations

Five career runs for the 3yo filly. Back from a 6-month break five weeks ago, a good 2nd of 11 in an AW maiden race - winner rated 91. She was only beaten a neck last August on fast turf ground in a strong-looking maiden race. An opening handicap mark of 73 looks very handy. Top jockey booked for the ride.
Second last time, distance and going to suit, good jockey and trainer, should be given serious consideration. Shortlist material, will be there at the business end of the race. Each way bet.

A J S Moore trained 3-year-old who has had 9 races on the flat, winning once and has finished in the frame 5 times. Her win came here at Windsor in July last year in a class 5 fillies stakes over 6f on good to firm going when making all to win by 1 3/4 lengths. She is in a class 5 handicap over 6f on good to firm going and has Joe Leavy in the saddle, who has ridden her before. She finished 3rd of 9 runners last time out here at Windsor 9 days ago when staying on at the finish, beaten 3 lengths. She is a c/d winner on similar going. Has a good e/w shout in this race today.

Race 1 at Windsor today is a Handicap (Class 5) for 3-year-olds over 1,218 m. The suggested wager is for the each way on the 3yo filly Alondra from the Charlie Hills yard, and she will be ridden by Jason Watson. This daughter of Sergei Prokofiev is a different kettle of fish since returning from a rest with 3 good efforts, including a win and improving all the while. She should be a major player here and should be included.
Really looks the one to beat here at Windsor. Top jockey booking looks intriguing as well. Down in trip and off a short break. Can't ignore the price, all things considered.

Very good 3rd on yard/seasonal debut before shaping better than bare form suggests last time out. Both tougher races than this and eased a pound with Jim Crowley back in the saddle. Looks good value at double-digit odds.

This horse is fast becoming my 'cliff horse,' but I'll give him one more try here. The run last time out was too bad to be true when Jamie Spencer and the vets were called in, but nothing came to light. Hopefully, the first-time visor and the first-time booking of Hector Crouch will see the horse return to form. This horse won a Class 2 novice on debut and was then sent off as the favorite in a Group 3. He was admittedly outclassed in that, but he's in handicaps now, racing off as low as 71. So anything like that level of form would see him win this without any fuss. Last chance saloon for him if he flops again here, though, I suspect.
LTO win at Chelmsford last month will give her much-needed confidence, but improvements are still required for her handicap debut. It helps that she has experience over C&D.

Winner of both of his starts so far, the first when coming from last position and the other when making all of the running. That shows that he is clearly a very adaptable type and he enters handicapping off what looks a workable opening mark.

Master Technician heads into Windsor with a solid record, having won three of his ten starts and placed in five. His recent fifth at Ascot over 7f was respectable, especially considering he was hampered during the race. Dropping back to 6f could play to his strengths, and with Oisin Murphy booked, he’s got a decent chance of being competitive in this field.

So Darn Hot has had four runs this year, all in C2, and won the first two. The latest was third on the second try off a 93. With a drop to C3 today off the same mark, it does put him top weight in this, but I think it could still be doable.
Rajaking looks a solid prospect here and can at least run well enough to grab a place. Has been running well and can improve on recent runs.
This is his toughest race to date, but he has been running well enough that he should be a safe each-way bet and could win if he improves a couple of pounds.
In a competitive handicap at Ascot last time out, I Maximus finished a creditable 6th. Clearly, the 6 furlongs is the animal's best trip, and another decent showing is expected at decent odds.

KING OF BEARS may have more to offer for the in form George Scott yard (Last 14 days: 5-28, 18%) now fitter on his third start of the season. He has won over 6f, has been dropped 6lb since last September, and may be ready to fulfill his potential. For a more detailed write-up please see my X feed.
Opened the season by winning at Bath over 1m4 in a similar handicap and was second last time out so clearly should be in the reckoning again.

This mare looks solid tonight. The yard is in form. The track and ground suit well. She's won off a pound higher mark, and last time's disappointment at Leicester could have been due to the track and distance. She's a confident choice.

Trojan Truth returns to Windsor looking to repeat last year’s win in this very race, running off the same mark of 55. He’s been a bit below par lately, finishing fourth in his last two starts, but the return of blinkers could sharpen him up. With a solid course record and conditions to suit, he’s got a fair shout of bouncing back to form.

The Mark Usher-trained 'This Time Maybe' hasn't got the best win-to-run ratio with just 1 win from 19 runs, but he does have 5 places. He was very slightly below par in his last run on the AW at Southwell at the end of April, where he didn't quite finish his race off after traveling like the winner turning in. However, he ran two excellent races immediately before, including winning at Wolverhampton in April. On those two runs, he should have a decent chance this evening off a mark of 53. Robert Havlin is a good jockey booking and is having his first ride on 'This Time Maybe'.

Bond Spirit mainly runs on the AW with a couple of turf runs each summer. He won off 50 on turf in May last year and was raised 4 lb. Since then, he hasn't won on the AW and his mark has drifted down. The long break is a concern, but if fit enough, he should run well off today's 46.

Westridge looks ready to strike again. He was just denied at Kempton last time, and now returns to the scene of his only career win. He’s still on a workable mark, and with conditions to suit, this looks like a great chance for him to go one better.
Has a couple of course and distance wins and, having bounced back to form last time out, Lingfield's current form may be hard to beat today.
This gelding mixes hurdling and the flat, and after a pipe opener last time and with his yard going well, tonight looks a good opportunity for him.
Rogue Supremacy 2yo with David o'meara making his debut here. The trainer had a 2yo winner last week, so he is taken to upset the favourite.
Won last race on good to firm. Distance no problem. Jockey taking three pounds off. Excellent chance. Should be there at the business end of the race. Each way bet.

Golden Rainbow has been knocking on the door lately and looks primed for a big run at Wetherby. He was only just denied at Redcar last time, finishing second by half a length, and now returns to a track where he’s gone well before. The extra half-furlong here should suit, and with a handy 3lb claim, he’s got a solid chance of going one better.

Only 2-33 but generally quite consistent at this sort of level. A bit below par so far this spring but has been competing in class 5s, so should appreciate this drop back into class 6 and is of interest this evening on that basis.

Golden Rainbow has been knocking on the door lately and looks primed for a big run at Wetherby. He was only just denied at Redcar last time, finishing second by half a length, and now returns to a track where he’s gone well before. The extra half-furlong here should suit, and with a handy 3lb claim, he’s got a solid chance of going one better.
Gogo Yubari has not been great since changing yards and moving up in trip to 6f on the AW. It's worth a shot that today's 5f+ and a change to turf with a drop to C6 could bring her back in EW.
Lady Mariko ran a career best when second at Nottingham and now makes her stable debut for a yard in form. If she builds on that effort, she’s got a strong chance of getting her head in front.
Reappeared over the extended mile at Beverley in April 2023 following a 6-month absence and will welcome this drop in trip.

Clasina has been knocking on the door with two solid runs this season. She was a close third at Musselburgh in April and followed that with another good effort at Wetherby. Still winless after 12 starts, but she’s racing off a workable mark and seems to be improving. If she continues on this upward trend, she could be in the mix.
Very strong EW bet. Having been dropped a pound after running into trouble last time and finishing full of running, would have been placed at least. Should go close.
Got off the mark in a handicap over this trip at Kempton in February. Was raised a hefty 8 lbs for that but now back down 4 lbs after 3 modest efforts subsequently. Fair chance in this company.

Jockey Jason Hart rode 3 winners at Chelmsford on Sunday and rides Kristal Klear for trainer Stella Barclay on Monday night. Ran poorly on last start at Southwell when last of 7 back in February and has not raced since. Obviously had a problem and returns in a race that lacks depth and if returning fit and well should be involved in the finish.

Didn't offer much last time out at Redcar, but QUEEN'S ROAD REVUE is considered now as she returns to the same trip and mark as a narrow fourth-placed finish back in April. That was in a class six, but this doesn't seem to be much more taxing, and I think there's potential for a big run if you are prepared to forgive the last time out misfire.
Runner-up last time out on the same race conditions as this evening. The trainer has a good-looking strike rate at this course, and this one could break its duck.
Comes from good sprinting stock, and with both jockey and trainer in good form too, has to have a solid chance.
Game Striker, a 2-year-old grey filly. A chance is taken with this Hugo Palmer newcomer. The trainer's 2-year-olds seem to be performing quite well. Nice each-way price.

Ran well last time out at Hamilton, beaten by just half a length, so comes here in decent form. That was his first run for some time, and with the cobwebs blown away, he should now be ready to get back to winning ways.
Still a maiden but looks like winning soon. Came 2nd last time out at Lingfield in a handicap and now tried in first-time headgear.

The trainer to follow when sending his runners to this course has a good strike rate from the 2-year-olds to the older horses. Although the odds suggest otherwise, I think this one has a value each-way chance.
Step up in trip is a positive sign here. Strong last run and shows he can handle himself. Think the distance should suit him better here and can go on to win if he gets the right run.
A very open race here, but Lights Go Down looks a major player in this race with an opening mark of sixty-four. It seems very generous given how well she has performed so far.
Very consistent this spring after reverting to turf from an all weather campaign. Ran well in defeat at Nottingham last time and should go close today while in this mood.

Only win came when just getting up over 5 furlongs at Newcastle in November. Has finished in the frame on all 5 subsequent outings, though has been a little disappointing the last twice.This looks a golden opportunity if anywhere near his best.
Captain Pickles came fourth last time at Hamilton and was unlucky in running, so worth another chance at a value-looking price here.
La Note Verte comfortably won a bumper at this meeting last year. She has not run since, but if fit and ready, she should provide another winner for Willie Mullins and Paul Townend.

The model I run has simulated this race and predicts Bearami Creek to win. Bearami Creek lines up here with the third highest RPR of this very large 17-horse field. All horses go out carrying the same initial amount of weight. Bearami Creek last raced 24 days ago and has race fitness coming into this. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator due to the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

The Willie Mullins mare La Note Vert is the obvious pick having won her bumper in good style but Gavin Cromwell's 
Sophia Rose might be capable of making the frame at long odds. She ran quite well in two bumpers, is nicely bred and her yard in very good form.

Rated 11 pounds clear of closest rival on official figures. Won or placed in all but one of his eight starts, seven of those better races than this (from Listed to Grade 1 company). Good run last time, only beaten by a stablemate, and the third has won easily since. Rivals here are out of form. Blood Destiny is smart and has youth on his side at six years old. This Willie Mullins (SR 33%) trained and Paul Townend (SR 25%) ridden selection (again) can get the job done.

Blood Destiny looks unbeatable bar accidents but The Banger Doyle is fit from the flat and a clear second best on ratings so looks the best bet the follow the favourite home or capitalise should the Mullins horse encounter any mishaps.

After a 2nd place in his last two runs, Game Point really should come out on top here over nine and a half furlongs. His outside draw should not be a problem as horses often run wide in the back straight at Gowran before cutting in around the bend.

Plenty to like about his racecourse debut at Gowran at the beginning of September when a close 2nd in a 7f maiden, staying on late in the day. Not disgraced on his return at Cork two starts ago, over a mile, when a close up 5th in a big field maiden. Ran poorly last time at Ballinrobe over 13f and can bounce back here dropping in distance with yard going well.
Finished second twice over a similar distance in Dundalk and May but did not fare so well in a handicap last month. So a return to something more familiar might suit.
Getting closer to a win after four performances to date. Was leading early on last time out at this course but didn't last out, finished 3rd, so drop in trip is the call today to aid her cause.

Dermot Weld's filly should appreciate the one mile this afternoon at Gowran Park and with first time blinkers I fancy Chocalho will challenge in this Fillies Maiden. Fourth on debut here and third last time out at Dundalk, I am siding with third time lucky for Chocalho.

The ground described as good can be swinging either way, being dry and with long grass that sees a slush wetness over it, or the other way where the rain has come and eased the surface but not quite soft. Today, with rain that has been around, might have eased the good ground without bringing soft into the equation. That can see this daughter of Kodi Bear putting her experience to good use, with an improved performance from her sixth-place debut run over course and distance just twelve days ago. Her last race and this looks competitive, but with connections having her out quickly, they must be seeing her being full of herself and primed to run.

Three or four have posted a decent showing or two but nothing spectacular so a chance is taken on the in form Gavin Cromwell's Camelot debutant In My Teens who has plenty going for her on paper and probably wont need to be anything special to get involved in the finish.

Quite a promising flat winner. He finished 11th out of 14 in a juvenile hurdle at Killarney 22 days ago, without being pushed hard. This result was underwhelming considering the potential he showed on his hurdles debut, but he poses a significant threat if he can recover his form.

By Golden Horn. Some half decent form at 1m 4f in the UK. Trip inadequate on Irish flat debut last time out. Now sent hurdling and should have a future in this sphere. Its not the strongest race so no surprise if this one takes some prize money home.

Higher Kingdom is an 8-year-old gelding trained by Adrian McGuinness. He is a six-time winner on the AW but yet to win in 27 starts on turf, which is a bit of a negative. However, he has been running well on turf of late. He was disappointing on his last start when a 5-1 favorite over CD, but he did get upset in the stalls, so that run can be forgiven. Previously, he finished 3/20 at Naas, only beaten a length behind Harry The Rogue, who has since finished 6-1-2 and is rated some 17lb higher in the ratings. He also has course form, finishing 2/17 at Gowran in September 22, and he should be more than capable of landing a blow in this contest under the experienced Jake Coen off a lowly handicap mark of 52.

Jazz Dreamers is now a seven-year-old and last won in August 2023. After finishing a decent 3rd of 15 at Roscommon in May on his first run for 11 months, the handicapper has generously dropped him two pounds to a mark of 52, which is four pounds below his last winning mark. He should go close with Joseph Harnett riding him again with a seven-pound allowance in this apprentice handicap.

ROCHESTER MIKE is surely the best treated runner lining up and his recent reappearance effort should have helped set him straight. An ex-Jessica Harrington-trained five year old who will have clearly enjoyed the best start to his racing life and by a leading sire in Wooton Bassett he looks set to go close.
Been running quite well in defeat for this jockey. Drop in trip a definite plus and should be in the mix off a feather weight today.

If there's a horse to improve significantly from 3 to 4 years old, I think it could be this one, especially given how well the stable's horses are running. Starts very nicely treated on pick. A 4 lbs claim is an extra boost, and first time out is probably the time to chance him fresher.
Not won since coming to Ireland, but did come 2nd at this course the time before last at least. The jockey has recently had a 40/1 winner and 25/1 2nd, so should be confident enough into the bargain.

I’ve backed SHARETHETREASURE twice now, and she’s left me with egg on my face. She stood up in the gates and missed the break LTO here, so forgiveness is required. I’m hoping the first-time visor can eke out a little improvement. The handicapper has been more than fair, shaving off another 3 lbs, leaving her at a career low..

Tim Doyle usually comes good with his runners this time of year. Lisabetta's two turf wins have come at this venue on good and heavy ground, so she will be happy regardless of the ground. She has a wide draw to overcome but races off 4lb lower than her last winning mark and is lurking near bottom weight. Could threaten for each-way money.

A notably talented filly from a distinguished yard. She has recorded 2 wins from 2 starts this year. She achieved her career best result by winning an 8 runner minor event at this course 12 days ago. She has a solid chance if she can continue her impressive form.

Would win this race easily on last season's form and could bounce back from a couple of under-par starts this term at group level. At the weights, rated 103, has a big chance if running anywhere near best form.
Consistent sort who has made the frame six times in his nine races. Acts on any surface and no reason why he shouldnt be in the mix again despite being seemingly the stables second string.
Bishopton has been placed three times in the last four runs since changing yards, with the latest being to second when second up after a break, which I think puts him in with an EW chance.

The favourite Shraheen could be opposable here as he hasn't run for 5 months and might need this. So the selection is Gavin Cromwell's Stuntman Steve, who has been running well recently. He has ruined his chances in his last 2 races with mistakes at vital times, and a good round of jumping can see him go close.

The model I run suggests Raydamann could win this race. Raydamann lines up here with the joint highest RPR of this 10-horse race and carries less weight than most of the competitors in this race. Prior distance winner over this 2m round trip. Looks to get over the line first here after reasonable form figures of 3213. Last ran 32 days ago. Model issued a 'very low' stake indicator which translates to a 0.5pt stake on a scale of 0-4.

A very dodgy one as a lot is taken on possibilities, but the horse has shown glimpses of ability. Whether today is the day, I don't know, but at the price, I'm willing to play. The horse has attracted the attention of the stewards a couple of times in maidens, and off bottom weight today 'might' be the day.

The model I run suggests Angelo Dundee should win this race. Angelo Dundee has the highest RPR of all the runners here and looks well placed to get over the line first. The additional weight being carried is relieved by the claiming jockey. Good second 19 days ago and can go one better here today. The model has issued a 'very high' stake indicator, which translates to a 4pt bet on a scale of 0-4.

Big Ned is a 5-year-old gelding trained by John Queally. He makes his bumper debut and is clearly well thought of, as he was sent off 5-2f in his only run in a PTP. He is the first foal out of the dam, The Brock Inn (IRE), who won a bumper, a flat race, and a 20-runner hurdle, posting a career-high RPR of 128. The trainer has had 19 winners in the last five years, and four have come in bumpers. His Big Ned may possess the necessary speed to be a big player, given his flat-based pedigree.

Third and fourth last month in handicaps around Gowran Park and Roscommon, and I fancy Sierra De Gredos will place again this afternoon back at Gowran. Off the same mark as last month's place here, I am siding with a competitive run from Sierra De Gredos.
Has won one and placed third in the other two of the last three runs. Has also won previously on similar going, so should be there or thereabouts today.
Down in trip and likes the surface. Slowly coming back to form, handles 1m well. Has a solid handicap form. Big price for a horse who has a lot of potential.

POPPADOM has run well at this track previously and his jockey will understand him and jnow what to expect having ridden him on multiple occasions. A four year old who brings plenty of experience and with this trip more likely to see him to best effect he rates a lilely type.

A chance is taken on Aoife's Territory making her handicap debut in a low grade handicap over 1 mile. The 4yo filly is by Territories out of a Dubawi mare so trip suits. Best of three maidens was the first and last of the three was seasonal debut last month. Dylan Kidd rides for trainer Pat Foley whose recent runners have gone close recently (small yard). Fair draw in stall 7. Wouldn't have to be a world-beater to go in on this first handicap start.

Money Dancer has been strong in the market and might well deliver on that. The selection has Colin Keane on board here, and that is always a plus. It ran well last time to finish fourth at Sligo, and the longer trip here will suit.

Beauparc won at Dundalk in April for his second career win, having won on turf handicap at Clonmel in September 23. His win at Dundalk was over 1m4f, and although disappointing back on turf at Sligo last month, that was over 1m2.5f, which is probably too short for her. Back over 12 furlongs from a 1lb lower mark, she looks like a good EW bet with 5 places on offer.
Rather fell out of the stalls last time out at Cork but still battled on to take third place and is generally quite consistent. Should be there or thereabouts.

Victoria Kesia is upped in trip here but if recent efforts are anything to go by she should be able to cope as she has been running on. The Murphy yard seems to be in decent nick at the moment and, as a bonus, there are extra places available here if she hits the crossbar.
Third last time out following up a win in a handicap at Southwell so has made a good start with a new yard and could perform well today.
Has won here over 1m and was really unlucky last time out when a neck 2nd after not finding a gap until too late over 1m 4f. Same distance and going today and looks a decent each-way chance at 18-1.

Has a strong rating and can't be ignored. Made all at Limerick and I think he will suit Gowran Park. Trip suits and is improving. The jockey upgrade he gets today can only help his cause. Yard believe in him.
The trainer has got 2 entered in this race, but his other runner is a reserve entry. They have got a good jockey booking/change, a good value each way bet for the 5 places available.

Itsallabouteve won at Tipperary in July and was placed on three other occasions last year. She was off a mark of 100 there and is just 2 lbs higher here. She has been runner-up on both previous runs at Listowel, including in this race last year, and looks a good each-way bet with four places on offer.
Weakened on th run in over 2m 2f at Downpatrick last time out but a ready winner on penultimate start over a shorter trip and has an obvious chance back at 2m here.

Adrian Sexton’s 8-year-old mare KATHERINE caught my eye six days ago at Ballinrobe. She was making up ground from off the pace, looking to be playing her hand perfectly, only to be denied room two from home. Despite this, the daughter of SHIROCCO kept plugging away valiantly to finish 5th.
She drops in class here and sheds 1lb, which is a positive, but the real standout (at least for me) is the quick turnaround of just six days. KATHERINE has done this only twice in her 38 career runs, winning one of those as recently as October last year, returning after just five days at Kilbeggan (16f, Good).
Jockey Sam Ewing remains in the saddle and brings a solid 32.43% place strike rate over the past month, along with a 29.55% place strike rate here in County Kerry over the last five years. The yard is taking a gamble, and I’m right there with them.

This is a very competitive race, but if we go simply on recent form, there's a lot to like about Ciao Adios. Still only a 6-year-old, the horse has fitness on her side, and with her typical hold-up tactics, she could do well here if there's a bit too much pace on.

Had form boosted off Naas 2nd at the beginning of April but disappointed at Tipperary last time. The reason is unknown, but another chance is taken on this mare with Sean O'Keefe riding a featherweight.

Impressive when stepped up to this distance for the first time when last seen. She won with more in hand than the length and a quarter margin when sent off favourite. Now that she has got her head in front, there should be plenty more to come from her with a 6lb rise looking fair.

Went in the tracker after winning a maiden back in April by 6l, running away from the pack on the opposite side of the track. I had already noted it from previous run when travelling well, but had saddle and/or equipment problems and at 25-1, was one of my very few winners last month. (at a price-missed it on here though) Ran in a class 1 race nto and ran ok for 9f, but tailed off last furlong and was 2nd lto after using a lot of energy making up ground after a slow start. H/c debut and looks weighted to do well.
This horse went close last time out. With winning form around this track and a very good draw today, I fancy this horse will go very close today.
In what looks like being a wide-open race, I am going to back Pink Oxalis, who is in great form with two wins on the bounce, including one here at Gowran Park, and should land the hat trick.
They are dropping this one back down in trip slightly with the same jockey on board. Also, adding the first-time tongue tie to the cheekpieces. A good value each-way bet for the 4 places available.

Pepper Noir looks interesting in this Gowran Park fillies' handicap. She has won 3 times on AW and ran her best race on turf when second at Leopardstown last month. She is off the same mark here and looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

A chance is taken on Fiver Friday at 25-1. She has been hurdling and won at Naas in her first hurdle in April. Last season, she had wins at Ayr, Hamilton, and Naas on the flat. Provided she avoids her habitual slow start, she could be competitive off her mark of 86 with Keithen Kennedy taking off five pounds.

Bit surprised to see this ex-French filly propping up the market on debut for Richard O'Brien. Her form is mixed but same can be said of her rivals and the booking of Billy Lee catches the eye. No forlorn hope.

The model I run suggests Bugs Moran should win this race. This result has been driven by Bugs Moran having the highest RPR of this 15-runner field. Bugs Moran goes out carrying the same weight as the majority of runners here, so not penalized for the higher potential. Comes here in reasonable form and looks to get back on top after a 5th place finish 21 days ago where the run was needed. The model has issued a 'very low' stake indicator as a result of the small gap back to second in the race simulation.

Was only 1/2l in front of Ontheropes last time and though a little worse off at the weights I'll suggest can confirm the placings dropping in trip. Won over 3m at Cork in April before finishing 3rd over 4f shorter and then followed that up by finishing 3rd again last time over 4f further. Dropping back to 3m makes sense and if that was the trip last time may well of beaten Ontheropes even further and at double the price of that one looks the value. Trainer going well with his few runners and though this one has contributed mostly to the following stats three winners from just six runners this year and the other three finishing 433 suggests this one looks the EW play back over a more suitable trip.

Won a point-to-point in March at Bandon over three miles. I fancy after finishing second last month in a Hunter's Chase at Killarney, the extra distance this evening at Listowel will suit the ten-year-old. Dundaniel won one of these in 2023 in Cork, and there is a lot to like about this assignment. I am siding with a good run and a top-three finish.

Although Whats New, ridden by Andrew Slattery, weakened from the lead and became unbalanced on the home straight on his previous visit to Gowran last year, his more recent runs elsewhere under apprentice riders have been more promising. He should stay the trip well and appears better held up.
Did nothing in three qualifying races but a good third when 50/1 on handicap debut and Colin Keane is booked to help ensure further progress.
Ventress is unplaced in all three starts so far but might well be a different proposition now stepping into handicap company. She might be better than an opening mark of 60 and can run well here.

Looked to want further as down the field in maiden over 7f but in top-class company at Listowel. Now returning from a 251-day layoff and on handicap debut. Trainer thinks highly of him, possible each-way squeak.

I am a big fan of the trainer, and Zuzzudios' run at Roscommon was full of promise. This is a good booking today as it's not harder, and there is a lot of deadwood here. I am thinking we are good for at least a place today.
J Harrington's entry that hasn't fired as yet had an apprentice riding previously. Now has Shane Foley in situ, upped in trip, and blinkers are on. Let the dabbling pay off.
